*Effective with the June 2016 report the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days were corrected to count the customer once if they have arrears in buckets for 60, 90 or 120 days.
Prior to June 2016 this data was not available and the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days included customers that may have had arrears in buckets for 60, 90 and 120 days.

Non-residential data 9d: Central Hudson is reporting the % of non-residential UNCOLLECTIBLE Accounts with Deposits, and not all non-residential accounts.
Effective with the November 2009 report, both Residential & Non Residential "reinstated DPA" includes renegotiated as well as reinstated

*Effective with the January 2016 report the dollars reported for residential data 5a (Reconnects Due to HEAP or DSS) represents the total dollar amount of HEAP or DSS assistance received.  
Prior to January 2016 this information was not available and the dollars reported were for the termination amount. 
*Effective with the June 2016 report the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days were corrected to count the customer once if they have arrears in buckets for 60, 90 or 120 days.
Prior to June 2016 this data was not available and the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days included customers that may have had arrears in buckets for 60, 90 and 120 days.

Notes: Beginning in May 2020, a change in methodology was implemented for calculating “Arrears Greater Than Sixty Days” for consistency with the reporting of other 
major gas and electric utilities in New York.  The new methodology uses the bill date in the calculation, whereas National Fuel had previously used the last date to pay

anticipated in both the number of termination notices and deferred payment agreements.

*Effective with the June 2016 report the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days were corrected to count the customer once if they have arrears in buckets for 60, 90 or 120 days.
Prior to June 2016 this data was not available and the count for the number of customers with arrears greater than sixty days included customers that may have had arrears in buckets for 60, 90 and 120 days.

MONTHLY  COLLECTIONS  REPORT
MONTHLY  COLLECTIONS  REPORT
Notes: Beginning in May 2020, a change in methodology was implemented for calculating “Arrears Greater Than Sixty Days” for consistency with the reporting of other 
major gas and electric utilities in New York.  The new methodology uses the bill date in the calculation, whereas National Fuel had previously used the last date to pay 
prior to the imposition of a late payment charge as the due date for purposes of this report.                                                                                                                    
During the COVID-19 shut off moratorium the Company decreased the collection threshold in order to allow more customers to apply for extended HEAP benefits.  A 
large increase was anticipated in both the number of termination notices and deferred payment agreements.
